rationale: Y engages directly with the ground truth's central thread — the gcanlin/R2-Y debate over cudagraph_mode belonging in the model vs. runner — and extends it with a concrete proposal to move the decision into the runner, plus a deeper finding that seeded requests lose reproducibility even at batch=1 under graph replay (extending the exact seed-under-cudagraphs concern gcanlin flagged). Y also ties talker_mtp_graph_safe/NPU gating to the failing NPU/AMD CI, closely mirroring Wallbreazzz's real NPU crash report. X is broader and well-evidenced but spends most of its comment budget on orthogonal issues (yaml capacity retune, stale docs, prefix-graph sibling profile, test coverage) that, while plausible, don't map onto what the actual reviewers cared about, and never engages the model-vs-runner architecture debate that dominates the ground truth. Both provide file:line anchors and no LATENT GAP CHECK section, so gap_hit is false for both; Y's suggested fixes are also more concrete (inline code patches) versus X's more hedged suggestions.
